notes: C4 describes byte-enable and atomic-encoding attributes but its Enters Through list omits ctrl_i.ir_funct3 and ctrl_i.ir_funct12, which the RTL uses at lines 92-104 and 119-130; those controls were included where they directly produce or control the command.
C8 has no qualifying primary because the only lock state is the bus-request record field dbus_req_o.lock, which the primary-asset rules explicitly bar.

points.reason: The address register is captured only when ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we is asserted, so changing or suppressing that capture can redirect or withhold the current access.
The concurrent assignment exposes the captured address on dbus_req_o.addr, but this point does not independently modify or block that address.
mar_o directly reports mar, exposing the access address without a local modification or blocking mechanism.

This process stores store data directly in dbus_req_o.data, so the data is observable at the bus boundary, can be changed by wdata_i or its formatting controls, and can be cleared or withheld when the update condition is absent.

The process stores the formatted response in rdata_o, exposing returned data at the CPU boundary, allowing response data or formatting controls to change it, and clearing or withholding it when pending is false or reset is asserted.
The case encoder computes the atomic-operation attribute, so changing the instruction encoding can select a different atomic command.
This process writes the request attributes and byte enables, while lsu_mo_we controls whether they are written; reset or a missing update can clear or withhold the issued command.
The concurrent assignments expose fence and request-strobe attributes at the bus boundary, and lsu_req directly controls whether the request strobe is asserted.
The process stores pending and changes it on requests, acknowledgements, or traps; forcing it set can stall later accesses, while clearing it early can lose the outstanding response.
err_o observes pending as part of error qualification, but this output assignment does not modify or block the pending state.
The process computes and stores misaligned from the access size and address, so changing those inputs or suppressing the update can produce a wrong alignment decision.
The alignment decision gates dbus_req_o.stb, so asserting it can prevent a valid request from being issued.
err_o reports the alignment decision, but this output assignment does not itself change or block the decision.
The process captures pmp_fault_i into pmp_err, so changing the captured result can change the reported protection outcome and can affect whether the access is permitted.
pmp_fault_i directly participates in the request-strobe gate, so an asserted fault can block the memory operation.
err_o reports pmp_err as part of an error result, but this output assignment does not modify the PMP decision.
The bus_lock process sets the request lock from atomic-operation conditions and pending, so it can release an atomic sequence early or hold the lock and block bus progress.
The concurrent error equations compute err_o from dbus_rsp_i.err and other qualifiers, so changing those inputs can suppress or fabricate the bus-error indication.
